title: Settlement 47-20 · Year 1
paragraphs: Under ordinary weather, the spring harvest brought 370 food into the settlement’s accounts. Under ordinary weather, the summer harvest brought 493 food into the settlement’s accounts. Under ordinary weather, the autumn harvest brought 411 food into the settlement’s accounts. Winter marked a change in the rhythm of the fields: the winter harvest record reports dormant crops and no crop food.

Work reached a milestone when hut #11 was completed in week 2. Work reached a milestone when field #12 was completed in week 4. At the following recorded harvest, that field contributed 83 food. Another 2 construction projects were completed; their records remain in the archive.

In week 1, reserves reached twelve weeks of current demand. In week 7, reserves fell below twelve weeks of current demand. In week 12, reserves reached twelve weeks of current demand. Storage limits took their own toll: 154 food was lost beyond capacity across this period. The accounts also record 30 stored food lost to spoilage.
The population records give the period a human measure: 1 death was recorded.
